title: OTLP bridge with selective span aggregation and loss‑tolerant replay
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a lightweight OTLP bridge service that performs tenant-aware selective span aggregation, partial-ack semantics, and a bounded loss-tolerant replay buffer to improve downstream export reliability to Jaeger/Tempo and other tracing backends. Goals: (1) reduce downstream connection churn by batching and coalescing small spans while preserving low tail-latency for sampled traces, (2) provide per-tenant adaptive buffering with TTL and memory caps to avoid noisy tenants causing OOMs, (3) implement partial acknowledgements so we can resume from last-successful-offsets and replay only missing envelopes, and (4) emit rich observability (export_latency, export_drop_rate, ack_lag, buffer_fill_pct) and per-tenant health signals for SLO-driven routing. The bridge must be protocol-compatible with OTLP gRPC/HTTP and translate to backend-specific envelopes for Jaeger/Tempo (span->trace conversion, tag normalization, and span-id padding for legacy clients). Design choices: admission control for bursts, dynamic sampling alignment with ingest sampler, and an opt-in per-tenant mode for strict at-least-once versus best-effort delivery. Rollout plan: unit + e2e tests against tempo-dev harness, shadow deployment for 2 weeks, canary in eu-west for low-traffic tenants, then ramp with per-tenant feature flags. Success metrics: reduce 5xx exporter errors by 70% on bursty workloads, maintain 95th percentile export latency under 200ms for hot traces, and keep memory per-instance under 2GB under normal load.
comments: 2025-02-11: Scoped initial prototype; validated OTLP gRPC streaming handshake behavior against tempo-dev. Observed reconnect storms when exporter auth fails — added exponential backoff + jitter.

2025-02-18: Design review with Platform and Observability teams. Feedback: make partial-ack state durable to avoid lost progress on restarts; prefer RocksDB over in-memory snapshots for offset store. Action: add durable offset store and encrypted WAL.

2025-02-25: POC tests: selective aggregation reduced per-span RPCs by 62% in synthetic microburst test. Memory footprint increased ~220MB due to per-tenant buffers; added eviction and tenant backpressure circuit breaker plan.

2025-03-01: Draft PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infer-observability/pulls/487. Needs integration tests with tempo + jaeger adapters. Requesting infra account to run e2e against staging tempo cluster (infra ticket INF-1153).

2025-03-04: Security review requested. Noted need for KMS encryption of offset WAL and stricter tenant isolation on multi-tenant hosts. Security flagged TLS client cert rotation for exporter connections as follow-up.

2025-03-05: Started implementing partial-ack replay logic; added unit tests for resume-from-offset and duplicate suppression. Next: stress test with 10k tenants simulated and add dashboards for per-tenant buffer pressure.
